hook_text: Three runners: 16 seconds, 15 seconds, 18 seconds. The biggest number wins, right? Wrong.
clip_script: Athletics day in Bloemfontein. 100 metres. Stopwatch: start, stop. Thabo 16 seconds. Lerato 15. Sipho 18. Who won? The shortest time! Lerato crossed first, so her watch stopped first. Now the 800 metres: 2 minutes 45 seconds. In seconds? 60 times 2 is 120, plus 45: 165 seconds. Then the wall calendar: thirty days has September, April, June and November. February, 28, or 29 in a leap year. 1 March is a Sunday? Count in sevens: 8, 15, 22 are Sundays too. So 24 March is a Tuesday. Time, measured and planned.
visual_style: Whiteboard stopwatch faces next to three runners; a calendar grid with Sundays in one column lighting up in sevens.
mood: Sports-day energy with a calendar twist.
pacing: Race puzzle, the reveal, the 800 m conversion, then the calendar trick.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and time how long it takes you to say the months of the year.
